n: The longest chapter in the Bible is a giant acrostic: 22 stanzas of 8 verses, one for each Hebrew letter, and every verse in a stanza starts with that letter. This first stanza (Aleph) opens like Psalm 1 — happy are those whose path is blameless.

f.g: Hebrew torah — instruction, teaching, not only rules.

n: Happiness belongs to those who keep God’s ‘testimonies’ and seek him wholeheartedly. Nearly every verse of this psalm uses one of about eight words for God’s word.

f.g: God’s solemn witness and covenant terms.

n: Such people avoid wrongdoing because they follow God’s paths. Obedience is pictured as walking a road.
The psalmist now speaks to God directly, as he will for the rest of the psalm: you commanded us to keep your ‘precepts’ carefully.

f.g: Specific instructions or charges given by God.

n: A sigh of longing: if only my life were steady in keeping your ‘statutes’! He knows his weakness and wishes for consistency.
When he pays attention to all God’s commandments, he won’t be put to shame.

f.g: Look carefully at; pay attention to.

n: As he learns God’s just rulings, he will praise him with an honest heart. Learning God’s ways leads to worship.
He resolves to obey, and pleads not to be abandoned. Determination and dependence go together.
Stanza Beth. How can a young person keep their life pure? By guarding it according to God’s word — a question every generation asks.
He has sought God with all his heart, yet still asks for help not to drift away.
He has treasured God’s word in his heart, like hiding a valuable, to guard against sin. Scripture memorized and pondered becomes protection.

f.w: Thy word have I hid in mine heart

n: He praises God and asks him to be his teacher — a request repeated often in this psalm.
He has spoken aloud all the rulings God has given. Sharing the word helps us keep it.

f.w: With my lips have I declared

n: Following God’s testimonies brings him as much joy as great wealth would.

f.w: as much as in all riches

n: He will think deeply about God’s instructions and keep his eyes on God’s paths.

f.g: Ponder, muse, speak quietly to oneself.

n: He will delight in God’s decrees and never forget his word.

f.w: I will not forget thy word

n: Stanza Gimel. He asks God to treat him generously so he can live and keep his word. Life itself is for obedience.
A beloved prayer: open my eyes to see wonders in your law. Understanding scripture requires spiritual sight that God gives.
He feels like a foreigner on earth, just passing through; God’s commandments are his guide in unfamiliar territory.

f.w: I am a stranger in the earth

n: His soul is crushed with constant longing for God’s rulings.
God rebukes the arrogant who stray from his commandments; they bring a curse on themselves.

f.g: The arrogant, insolent — a recurring enemy in this psalm.

n: He asks God to roll away the scorn others heap on him because of his faithfulness.
Even powerful officials plotted against him, but he kept meditating on God’s decrees. Faith doesn’t wait for opposition to stop.
God’s testimonies are his delight and his ‘counsellors’ — literally ‘men of my counsel,’ his trusted advisers.
Stanza Daleth. His soul clings to the dust — he feels flattened, near death. ‘Quicken’ means give life; he asks God to revive him.
He told God everything about his life, and God answered. Now he asks for teaching.

f.g: I have openly told you my life, confessing all.

n: If God helps him understand, he will talk about God’s wonders. Understanding leads to testimony.
His soul weeps or drips away with sorrow. He asks God to strengthen him through his word.

f.g: Drips away with grief, like tears.

n: He asks God to keep him from deceptive ways and to graciously give him his law.
He has chosen the way of faithfulness and set God’s rulings before him like a guide.

f.w: I have chosen the way of truth

n: He has clung to God’s testimonies; he asks not to be disappointed.

f.g: Clung to — the same Hebrew word as ‘cleaveth’ in v. 25.

n: When God enlarges his heart — gives it understanding and freedom — he will run eagerly in the way of the commandments, not just trudge.

f.g: Broaden my understanding; set me free.

n: Stanza He. Every verse here is a request. ‘Teach me your way, and I will keep it to the end.’
Give me understanding, and I will obey wholeheartedly. True obedience comes from understanding, not mere compliance.
Lead me along the path of your commandments, for I delight in it.
Turn my heart toward your testimonies, not toward greed. The heart has to be pointed somewhere.
Turn my eyes away from worthless things, and give me life in your way. What we look at shapes who we become.
Confirm your promise to your servant, who is devoted to revering you.
Take away the disgrace I dread, for your judgments are good.
He has longed for God’s instructions; he asks for new life through God’s righteousness.

f.g: Give me life by your saving justice.

n: Stanza Vau. Let your covenant love and salvation come to me, as you promised.

f.w: thy salvation, according to thy word

n: Then he will have an answer for those who taunt him, because he trusts God’s word.
He asks God never to take the word of truth from his mouth — never let him lose his testimony.
So he will keep God’s law always — ‘continually for ever and ever.’

f.g: The piled-up words stress unbroken constancy.

n: He will walk freely, in wide open space, because he seeks God’s precepts. Obedience brings true freedom.
He will speak of God’s testimonies even before kings, without shame.
God’s commandments, which he loves, are his delight.
He will lift his hands toward God’s commandments — a gesture of prayer, reverence, and eager reaching.

f.w: My hands also will I lift up

n: Stanza Zain. ‘Remember your word to me’ — the promise that gave him hope. Faith rests on God’s promises.

f.w: Remember the word unto thy servant

n: His comfort in suffering is that God’s word has given him life.

f.w: This is my comfort in my affliction

n: Arrogant people have mocked him terribly, but he has not turned aside from God’s law.
Remembering God’s ancient rulings — his past faithfulness — comforts him.
He is seized with burning anger — ‘horror’ — at those who abandon God’s law.

f.g: Burning indignation, a hot wind of anger.

n: God’s decrees have been his songs in the house where he lives as a pilgrim — this temporary earthly life.
He remembers God’s name even at night, and keeps his law.
This blessing has been his because he kept God’s precepts — or, ‘this has been my practice: keeping your precepts.’

f.g: This has been mine — this has been my way of life.

n: Stanza Cheth. The Lord is his ‘portion’ — his share of the inheritance. Like the Levites, who received no land, his treasure is God himself.
He sought God’s favor with his whole heart — literally ‘I stroked your face,’ an idiom for earnestly seeking favor.
He reflected on his life and turned his feet back to God’s testimonies. This is repentance: thinking, then turning.
He hurried and did not delay in obeying. Postponing obedience is a quiet form of disobedience.
The cords or gangs of the wicked have entangled and robbed him, but he hasn’t forgotten God’s law.

f.g: Cords, ropes; or bands of robbers.

n: He gets up at midnight to give thanks — like Paul and Silas singing in prison at midnight.
He is a friend of all who revere God and keep his commands. Good companions strengthen faith.
The whole earth is full of God’s covenant love; he asks to be taught.

f.w: The earth, O LORD, is full of thy mercy

n: Stanza Teth. Every verse begins with the letter for ‘good.’ God has dealt well with his servant, just as he promised.
He asks for good judgment and knowledge, because he trusts God’s commandments.
Before affliction he wandered; now he keeps God’s word. Hard times can bring us back.

f.w: Before I was afflicted I went astray

n: ‘You are good and do good’ — a simple, deep statement of God’s character.
The arrogant smeared him with lies, but he keeps God’s precepts with his whole heart.

f.g: Smeared, plastered over — as with a coat of lies.

n: Their hearts are dull and insensitive, like fat; but he delights in God’s law.
It was good for him to be afflicted, so he could learn God’s statutes. Suffering became a school.

f.w: It is good for me that I have been afflicted

n: God’s instruction is worth more than thousands of pieces of gold and silver.

f.w: better unto me than thousands of gold

n: Stanza Jod. God made and shaped him with his own hands; now he asks for understanding to learn God’s commands. The Creator is also the Teacher.
Other believers will be encouraged to see him, because he has waited on God’s word.

f.w: will be glad when they see me

n: He acknowledges that God’s rulings are right and that God afflicted him in faithfulness — even trials come from a faithful God.
He prays for God’s covenant love to comfort him, as promised.
Let your tender compassion come to me so I may live; your law delights me.

f.g: Deep compassion, like a mother’s love.

n: May the arrogant be ashamed for wronging him with lies; he will keep pondering God’s precepts.

f.g: Twisted the truth to wrong me.

n: He asks that fellow believers — those who know God’s testimonies — would turn to him in fellowship.
May my heart be whole and blameless in your statutes, so I’m never ashamed.
Stanza Caph — the low point of the psalm. His soul faints with longing for God’s salvation, but he still hopes in his word.
His eyes are worn out from watching for God’s promise: ‘When will you comfort me?’
He feels like a leather wineskin hung near the fire — shriveled, blackened, and useless. Yet he does not forget God.

f.g: A leather wineskin dried and cracked by smoke.

n: How many days does he have left? When will God bring justice against his persecutors?

f.w: How many are the days of thy servant?

n: The arrogant dug pits to trap him — in defiance of God’s law.
God’s commands are faithful, while his persecutors are false. ‘Help me!’
They nearly wiped him off the earth, but he didn’t abandon God’s precepts.
He asks for renewed life through God’s steadfast love, so he can keep God’s testimony.
Stanza Lamed — the turning point. God’s word stands firm forever in heaven, unshaken by earthly trouble.

f.w: thy word is settled in heaven

n: God’s faithfulness spans all generations; he founded the earth and it stands.
Heaven and earth continue by God’s ordinances, for all creation serves him.
If God’s law had not been his delight, he would have died in his suffering.
He will never forget God’s precepts, because through them God gave him life.

f.w: with them thou hast quickened me

n: ‘I am yours — save me.’ Belonging to God is the basis of his plea.
The wicked lie in wait to destroy him, but he focuses his mind on God’s testimonies.
Everything earthly, however perfect, has limits; but God’s commandment is boundless.

f.g: A limit to every human achievement.

n: Stanza Mem. ‘Oh, how I love your law!’ He thinks about it all day — the emotional heart of the psalm.

f.w: O how love I thy law!

n: God’s commandments, always with him, make him wiser than his enemies.

f.w: for they are ever with me

n: Meditating on God’s testimonies gives him more insight than all his teachers.

f.w: more understanding than all my teachers

n: Obedience has given him more understanding than even the elders. Wisdom comes by living the truth, not age alone.
He has kept his feet from every evil path so he can keep God’s word.
He has not turned from God’s rulings, because God himself has taught him.
God’s words taste sweeter than honey — not a burden but a delight.

f.w: sweeter than honey to my mouth

n: God’s precepts give him understanding, so he hates every false path.
Stanza Nun. One of scripture’s best-known verses: God’s word is a lamp for my feet and a light for my path. Ancient lamps lit only the next few steps — enough to keep walking.

f.w: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet

n: He has made a solemn vow, and will keep it: to obey God’s just rulings. Covenants are promises we follow through on.

f.w: I have sworn, and I will perform it

n: He is deeply afflicted, and asks God to revive him as promised.
He offers his words of praise as a voluntary sacrifice, asking God to accept them and teach him.
His life is constantly ‘in his hand’ — always at risk — yet he doesn’t forget God’s law.

f.w: My soul is continually in my hand
f.g: Idiom: my life is constantly in danger.

n: The wicked set traps for him, but he didn’t stray from God’s precepts.
God’s testimonies are his inheritance forever — the joy of his heart.
He has set his heart on doing God’s decrees always, to the very end.
Stanza Samech. He hates double-minded, divided loyalty, but loves God’s law. ‘Vain thoughts’ likely means half-hearted people.

f.g: Possibly ‘the double-minded’ — those divided in loyalty.

n: God is his hiding place and his shield; he waits in hope for God’s word.
He tells evildoers to leave him alone — he will keep God’s commandments.
Hold me up as you promised, so I may live and not be let down in my hope.
With God holding him up he will be safe, and will keep his eyes on God’s statutes.

f.w: Hold thou me up, and I shall be safe

n: God rejects all who stray from his statutes; their deceptions are empty lies.
God removes the wicked like ‘dross’ — the impurities skimmed off melted metal. That is why he loves God’s testimonies.
His body shivers in awe of God, and he reverences God’s judgments.
Stanza Ain. He has done what is just and right, and asks not to be left to oppressors.
‘Be surety for thy servant’ — guarantee his welfare, as someone who co-signs for a debt. Christ is called the ‘surety’ of a better covenant.

f.g: Stand as guarantor; pledge yourself for me.

n: His eyes are worn out watching for God’s salvation and his righteous promise.

f.w: Mine eyes fail for thy salvation

n: Treat your servant according to your covenant love, and teach me.
‘I am your servant’ — so give me understanding to know your testimonies.
It is time for the Lord to act, because people have broken his law. Latter-day revelation likewise urges urgent labor in the last days.

f.w: It is time for thee, LORD, to work

n: Therefore he loves God’s commandments more than gold, even the purest gold.
Therefore he counts all God’s precepts right in every matter, and hates every false path.

f.g: In everything — the whole of God’s word.

n: Stanza Pe (‘mouth’). God’s testimonies are wonderful, so his soul keeps them.
When God’s words enter — or are ‘opened up’ — they bring light and understanding even to the simple.

f.w: The entrance of thy words giveth light

n: He opened his mouth and panted like a thirsty animal, longing for God’s commands.
Turn to me and be gracious, as you always do for those who love your name.

f.g: As is your custom, your habit.

n: Make my steps steady by your word, and let no sin rule over me.

f.g: Make my steps firm and directed.

n: Free me from human oppression, and I will keep your precepts.
Let your face shine on your servant — an echo of the priestly blessing.
Rivers of tears flow from his eyes because people don’t keep God’s law. Love for God includes grief over sin.

f.w: Rivers of waters run down mine eyes

n: Stanza Tzaddi (the letter for ‘righteous’). The Lord is righteous, and his judgments are upright.
The testimonies God commanded are righteous and completely faithful.
His zeal burns him up because his enemies ignore God’s words. Jesus’ disciples recalled a similar line when he cleansed the temple.
God’s word is refined and pure like tested metal, so his servant loves it.
He is small and despised, but doesn’t forget God’s precepts. Faithfulness doesn’t depend on status.
God’s righteousness is everlasting, and his law is truth.
Trouble and anguish have seized him, yet God’s commandments are his delight.
God’s testimonies are righteous forever. ‘Give me understanding, and I will live.’

f.w: give me understanding, and I shall live

n: Stanza Koph. He cries out with his whole heart for an answer, and promises obedience.

f.w: I cried with my whole heart

n: ‘I cry to you; save me, and I will keep your testimonies.’
‘Prevented’ means ‘came before’: he was up before dawn, crying for help and hoping in God’s word.
His eyes are open before each night watch so he can meditate on God’s word through the night.

f.g: Divisions of the night when guards changed.

n: Hear me by your steadfast love; give me life according to your just ways.
Those who pursue evil draw near to attack him, but they are far from God’s law.
The enemies are near — but God is nearer. All his commands are true.
He has long known that God established his testimonies to last forever.
Stanza Resh. Look at my suffering and rescue me, for I have not forgotten your law.
‘Plead my cause’ — be my defense attorney. ‘Redeem me and give me life.’
Salvation is far from the wicked, because they don’t seek God’s statutes.

f.w: Salvation is far from the wicked

n: God’s compassions are great; give me life according to your just decrees.
Though persecutors are many, he doesn’t turn from God’s testimonies.
He looked at the faithless and felt disgust, because they don’t keep God’s word.
‘See how I love your precepts’ — give me life by your steadfast love.

f.w: Consider how I love thy precepts

n: The ‘sum’ or whole of God’s word is truth, and every just ruling lasts forever.

f.g: Or ‘the sum’ — the entirety of your word.

n: Stanza Schin. Rulers persecute him without cause, but his heart trembles in awe only before God’s word.

f.w: standeth in awe of thy word

n: He rejoices over God’s word like someone discovering great treasure taken in battle.

f.w: as one that findeth great spoil

n: He hates and detests lies, but loves God’s law.
Seven times a day he praises God — seven meaning complete, continual praise.

f.g: Seven symbolizes fullness; praise all day long.

n: Those who love God’s law have great peace, and nothing makes them stumble. ‘Offend’ here means cause to trip.
He has waited for God’s salvation while doing his commandments — hope and action together.

f.w: I have hoped for thy salvation

n: His soul keeps God’s testimonies and loves them deeply.
He keeps God’s instructions because his whole life is open before God.

f.w: all my ways are before thee

n: Stanza Tau, the last letter. He prays that his cry will reach God and bring understanding.

f.w: Let my cry come near before thee

n: May my plea reach you; rescue me as you promised.
When God teaches him, praise will pour from his lips like a bubbling spring.
His tongue will sing of God’s word, for all God’s commands are right.

f.w: My tongue shall speak of thy word

n: He has chosen God’s precepts, so he asks for God’s helping hand.
He longs for God’s salvation and delights in his law.

f.w: I have longed for thy salvation

n: Let me live so I can praise you, and let your rulings help me.
A humble ending: after 175 verses of devotion, he admits he has wandered like a lost sheep and asks God to come find him. Jesus is the Good Shepherd who seeks the lost.

f.w: I have gone astray like a lost sheep
